title: Amplitude & Frequency
description: Echo Bot displays a sound as a wiggly wave. Learn to read its two key measurements — amplitude and frequency — to unlock fragment 5.

content.value: A vibration repeats over and over. One complete back-and-forth motion is called an OSCILLATION. We can picture a sound as a wave, and two measurements describe it: amplitude and frequency.
AMPLITUDE is the size of the vibration — how far the object moves from its rest position. A big, wide vibration has a large amplitude; a small, gentle one has a small amplitude.
FREQUENCY is how many oscillations happen each second. It is measured in HERTZ (Hz). A frequency of 100 Hz means 100 complete vibrations every second. Faster vibration = higher frequency.

AMPLITUDE → how BIG the vibration is (height of the wave)
FREQUENCY → how FAST it vibrates, in hertz (Hz)

1 Hz = 1 complete oscillation per second
50 Hz = 50 oscillations every second
Don't mix them up! Amplitude is about SIZE of the swing; frequency is about SPEED (how many per second). They control different things about the sound — you'll see how next module.
Key Takeaway: A sound wave is described by its amplitude (size of the vibration) and its frequency (number of oscillations per second, measured in hertz, Hz).
